tasks.category: Leadership Level 3, Leader of People (Develop Intent)
tasks.verbatim_text: Leaders of people have increasing challenges. They accept responsibility, not only for their own actions, but for those of their team. Leaders of people act to develop credibility as leaders: placing the team ahead of themselves, demonstrating trustworthiness, mastering essential technical skills, and instilling the values of the organization in their teams.
Gather critical state, regional, and local emergency medical sy stem (EMS) resource information, regulations, and response capabilities.

Coordinate with the Logistics Section Chief (LSC) and other functional areas to order emergency response personnel with necessary capabilities and equipment consistent with the current and projected scale of the incident.
Establish partnerships with local and regional EMS, hospitals, he alth clinics, search and rescue teams, fire departments, and public health officials.
Validate licensure, qualification, and readiness of assigned personnel and equipment.
Provide leadership on incident medical resource decision making.
Make daily division assignments for medical unit staff and provide supervision for medical resources.
Ensure medical unit staff adhere to proper timekeeping, work-rest ratio, and other applicable guidance defined in the NWCG Standards for Interagency Incident Business Management, PMS 902.

tasks.category: Perform Medical Unit Leader- Specific Duties
tasks.verbatim_text: Develop and maintain a Medical Plan (ICS 206 WF) to assist with an Incident Within an Incident (IWI) response.

tasks.category: Perform Medical Unit Leader- Specific Duties
tasks.verbatim_text: Maintain 24-hour emergency response readiness.

tasks.category: Perform Medical Unit Leader- Specific Duties
tasks.verbatim_text: Establish, manage, and maintain medical unit aid station(s).
Communicate and coordinate with local, regional, and state medical resources.
Establish and maintain positive internal and external interpersonal working relationships.
Consult with public health officials on response to medical em ergencies that have the potential for a significant number of patients (e.g., communicable disease outbreak).
Coordinate with safety and operations functional areas.
Coordinate with the Facilities Unit Leader (FACL) to provide and maintain utilities, space, and facilities.
Coordinate with the Compensation/Claims Unit Leader (COMP) fo r patients with injuries or illness requiring care outside the medical unit aid station.
Coordinate with the Communications Unit Leader (COML) and Radio Operator (RADO) regarding IWI procedures.
Account for and monitor the health, safety, and welfare of assigned incident personnel.
Anticipate staffing needs; ensure an appropriate level of medical su pport providers are available and staged appropriately throughout the incident.
Ensure adequate personnel and equipment resources are available for emergency medical evacuation of patients from remote areas.
Ensure that the Medical Plan (ICS 206 WF) is current and m edical responders are briefed with updated communication procedures and transportation plans.
Complete, authorize, and ensure timely submission of medical unit documentation through proper channels.
Maintain all required incident documentation generated through operation of the incident medical unit.
Properly dispose of any Personally Identifiable Information (PII)/ Protected Health Information (PHI) at the end of the incident.
Anticipate demobilization, identify excess resources, and co ordinate with your incident supervisor to prepare the demobilization schedule.
